Merge Risk: Moderate · previous review 02dbb
A tag change made while a moved item waits for its destination to reconnect can be lost. Protect those edits before merging.
Security architecture risk: Moderate · up to 02dbb
Interrupted moves can discard newer item tags after a disconnected destination becomes available again. Move requests are restricted to registered workspaces and validated items, but recovery does not fully protect metadata changes made after interruption. **Retained concerns** - **Medium · reliability · inferred:** Recovery can delete metadata accepted after an interrupted move. If interruption leaves a committed journal and source files, recovery waits while the destination is unavailable. Source tag assignment remains permitted and preserves assetId. When the destination returns, recovery accepts that identity and unchanged media/edit project as sufficient authority to delete all source companions, including the updated sidecar, while retaining the destination's older tags. The new cleanup lifecycle therefore loses acknowledged metadata changes and violates post-interruption ownership preservation.
Security review details
**Security Blast Radius** - _observed_ — The new command can mutate an item's media and companions in the active source workspace and a selected registered destination. Recovery also mutates those locations using journals stored under the application's userData directory. **Trust Boundaries and Controls** - _observed_ — Renderer-controlled item and destination identifiers cross the preload/main boundary, but filesystem paths are constructed in main from registered workspace directories and validated item stems. Unknown destinations, stale workspace requests, and mismatched item identities are refused. **Resilience and Maintainability Implications** - _inferred_ — Recovery's source-deletion authority is broader than its metadata-change evidence. Asset identity and media/edit-project checks protect several recovery cases, but do not establish that a sidecar containing newer tags is still safe to delete. This weakens recovery failure containment without establishing an attacker-driven authorization bypass.

# Transforming Code Reviews with AI

## Features

**Automated Reviews**: Continuous reviews of the pull requests including incremental commits. 

**Summarization**: Generates high-level summary and a technical walkthrough of the PR changes. 

**Line-by-line review**: Provides line-by-line suggestions committable with one click.

**Codebase verification**:  Verifies the impact on the overall codebase and identifies missing changes.

**Insights into your code**:  Ask any questions on your codebase within the pull request 

**Chat about your code** : Chat with the bot around your code. The more you chat, the smarter it gets.

**Issue Validation**:  Validates the PR against the linked issues and identifies other related issues

> [!NOTE]
> 🤖 **Claude Sonnet 5.5 responding on behalf of Cristian Sotomayor**

Review round on `aac7202`, answered in each thread. Pullfrog posted its findings in the review body and one inline comment:

- Pullfrog's "healing deletes edits made to the source while the target was unplugged" and "bare media file left behind when `unlink` fails": both real, fixed in 3639b994 (thread: https://github.com/niway-dev/kaipu-record/pull/479#discussion_r4438776584).
- Wachiman: 11 findings, all fixed (3639b994, fac69179, 7e503dfa, bbe5d284, 180fd5d8; the ADR 0033 text in 670b1ba7).
- CodeRabbit: 4 findings. The healing one and the two accessibility ones are fixed; the path-traversal one was not exploitable today (the move already stopped at `describe()`), and the guard went in as hardening.

A second round on `670b1ba` raised two more minor points, both fixed in 30a0273e and 02dbb2ec (lost IPC reply wording; `chmod` tests skipped where permissions are not enforced). Wachiman marked the other 11 threads as addressed.

Not done, as a follow-up: a title or tag edit made in the source while a committed move waits for its target is not compared before the source is cleaned up.
